messages.subject: STAN Code for Parametric Nonlinear Model (Serial Dilution Assay Example, BDA3-19.1)
parts: The parametric nonlinear model example given in Gelman et al. (2004) and summarized in BDA3 Example 19.1 is very interesting. I would like to learn more about how the parameter estimation and inference is done using STAN. Does anyone know if there is publicly available STAN code performing the steps discussed in the example? The BDA3 site doesn't look to have anything related to the model for Example 19.1.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Stan Code for Parametric Nonlinear Model (Serial Dilution Assay Example, BDA3-19.1)
parts:
I don't think anyone's contributed Stan code for this.
And I can't find Andrew's BUGS code, which I find is usually
easier to understand for me than the narrative description
in BDA and the original paper. The original paper is here, but no
references to any extra material I saw offhand:

http://www.stat.columbia.edu/~gelman/research/published/serial.pdf

It looks like it'd be straightforward to code.

The model would just be

parameters {
real<lower=0,upper=1> alpha;
vector<lower=0>[4] beta;
...

model {
for (i in 1:N) {
real g;
real sd;
g <- beta[1] + beta[2] / (1 + (x[i] / beta[3])^(-beta[4]));
sd <- (g / A)^alpha * sigma_y;
y[i] ~ normal(g, sd);
...
}

You need to declare the other parameters and priors, and then do some
more work for the dilution errors section, which I didn't read in enough
depth to understand. But I think you can build the model up in stages,
starting with no dilution error.

- Bob

P.S. STAN -> Stan; it's not an acronym.
